completion_criteria.text: hooks/lib/pre-tool-use.mjs inverted to deny-by-default inside a protected root: any resolvable token under a protected root DENIES unless the segment head is on an explicit read-only allowlist. shell-tokens.mjs left unchanged.

Both directions proven by committed tests: all 12 verified evasions (including `( rm -rf <root> )` and `sudo rm -rf <root>`) assert DENY, and the 41-command read-only corpus asserts ALLOW. Red-before/green-after evidence recorded.
The scanSegments blow-up resolved so the guard fails CLOSED on oversized or pathological input, never open, with a test asserting the fail-closed path at the boundary.
Full plugin test suite green on the branch, and a fresh code-reviewer plus security-reviewer pass over the final diff returns no CRITICAL or HIGH findings.

Branch merged to main, plugin published to the marketplace, and re-installed globally - then a live end-to-end check against the real store shows a real evasion DENIED and ordinary read commands still ALLOWED.

open_risks: CRITERION 4 NOT MET AT HEAD; THIS THREAD CANNOT CLOSE AS WRITTEN. Criteria are fixed at creation under the DoD gate. 1-2 describe the parser 0029 deleted; 3 names scanSegments, deleted; 5 asserts DENY where the tripwire answers ask. Disposition is create_successor, not an in-place rewrite.

UNRESOLVED, needs a user call: Round B used git add -A and swept Round A in-flight files into 3 commits. No content lost, suite green; damage is attribution only. src/util/git-env.mjs exists ONLY in 8962003, whose message is about the tripwire. All 30 commits unpushed. Later rounds used pathspecs.

ALL VERIFICATION IS macOS, git 2.55.0, Node 26.4.0, ONE MACHINE. Unverified on Windows and older git: resolve() on UNC paths in the guard root check, ABSENT_HOOKS_PATH under the Windows null device, devNull as GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, -c core.hooksPath quoting. git init -b needs git 2.28+.
PROMPT FATIGUE is still the guard's real failure mode and is security-relevant, since the prompt IS the protection. Documented in the README, but no test pins the count of newly-prompting commands.

The drift-signals gpg flake is REDUCED, NOT FIXED. Ledger commits no longer invoke gpg, but test/e2e/helpers/fixtures.mjs sets no commit.gpgsign=false, so the suite's own project commits still run real gpg. One-line fix, left out of scope.

Under a NON-DEFAULT ledger_branch the guard offers nothing, and this SHARPENED under verification: on the DEFAULT orphan-branch backend a custom branch resolves to refs/heads/<branch>, which the guard never checks. Only custom-ref is partially mitigated.
rm -rf .git && git init still destroys the ledger ref unprompted. Deliberately not trigger-covered per 0043; documented in the README.

Sandbox hooks/MCP question remains UNVERIFIED per 0037. Recoverable-history writes happen from an MCP server process, so if MCP servers are subject to denyWrite, a denyWrite entry over the ledger root stops the plugin writing its own store. The test is a human action.
UNAUTHORIZED DEFECT, open, do not fix without explicit go: the Stop hook nags every turn (stop.mjs exits 2 unconditionally, never reads stop_hook_active). Surfaced three times now with no user reply.

Shell parsing, tokenization, allowlisting or head normalization in ANY form (0029). Per 0054 this also covers the /t substring case: accepted cost, not a defect.
The other four canonical stores; future rollout, per-repo.
ledger-cli sync and publication of the _ledger ref. LocalDriver.sync() stays {synced:false}.
The one-line commit.gpgsign=false in the e2e fixture that would finish the drift-signals flake.
